### BACKLOG-310 — `/logger` Page Client-Side Crash: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isTTY')`

**Status:** OPEN, unverified in a real browser — found delegated session `brixsports-v2-fa`, 2026-08-27/28, while live-verifying `BACKLOG-252`.
**Priority:** flagged as potentially CRITICAL pending confirmation — if this is a real bug rather than an automated-browser artifact, it breaks the actual live match-logging UI for every real logger.
**Problem:** navigating to `/logger?matchId=<real UPCOMING match with published lineups>` against the local dev server consistently (reproduced on repeat) rendered a full-page "500 / Application error" with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isTTY')`. Traced via `read_console_messages` to originate inside React DOM's dev-mode webpack client bundle (`react-dom-webpack-client.browser.development.js`), caught by the `<ClientPageRoot>` error boundary — **not** inside any app source file (`grep -r isTTY src/` returns zero matches). Did not reproduce on `/admin` or the public home page in the same session.
**This session's working theory (not proven):** the automated Browser-pane tool used for this session's verification work is tripping some Next.js Fast Refresh / dev-overlay code path that expects a real terminal/stdio environment (`isTTY` is a Node `process.stdout`/`stderr` property, not normally something client-side React code touches directly — suggests dev-only tooling, not production code). `/logger` renders an unusually heavy client component tree (`FootballLogger.tsx`, WebSocket setup, offline queue, multiple dynamic imports) relative to the two pages that didn't crash, which is consistent with a dev-overlay/HMR edge case being more likely to surface there, but this is circumstantial, not confirmed.
**Why not fixed or dismissed here:** no app code was found to be the cause, so there's nothing in `src/` to point a fix at yet. Equally, "probably just the automation tooling" is a judgment call under time pressure, not a verified conclusion — this needs a real, non-automated browser (a human, or a different verification path) to confirm whether `/logger` genuinely loads correctly in production/normal dev conditions before this is closed as a non-issue.
**Workaround used to complete `BACKLOG-252`'s own smoke test:** bypassed the page entirely, called the real event-logging API directly via the Browser pane's authenticated `fetch()` — see `BACKLOG-252`'s evidence block. That confirms the underlying API path is healthy; it says nothing about whether the actual logger-facing UI is.

**Update — session `brixsports-v2-37`, 2026-08-28: independently reproduced, dev-overlay theory very likely WRONG.** Reproduced on a completely separate Browser-pane instance, against `https://brixsports-staging.vercel.app/logger?matchId=ZMBbLfLIoXVCkgJv7c8j2` — a real production-built Vercel deployment, not a local `next dev` server. Vercel deployments run `next build`, which does not ship Fast Refresh/dev-overlay code at all — so the original theory (an automated tool tripping dev-only tooling) cannot explain a crash on a production bundle. Same exact error reproduced: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isTTY')`, thrown inside client chunk `3609-c6a2aafdbbf385ac.js` (uncaught, `__sentry_captured__: true`), caught by the app's real `src/app/error.tsx` boundary — confirmed via screenshot this is the styled "Houston, we have a problem" 500 page, not a raw crash. Auth state at the time of repro was an already-authenticated admin session (not the intended logger token — a separate cookie-injection limitation in this environment), so the crash is not obviously role-gated; worth confirming as a genuine logger session next.

**Root-cause search started, not completed:** `grep -r isTTY src/` still returns zero — confirmed again this session, not just carried over. Attempted to pull the actual crashing chunk (`3609-c6a2aafdbbf385ac.js`) directly from staging and grep it for the literal string `isTTY` — **zero matches**, meaning either minification renamed/obscured the property access, or the throw originates in a *different* chunk than the one grepped (the console trace also names `webpack-...js` as an earlier frame, not checked yet). Candidate suspects from `package.json`, not yet individually confirmed: any Node-only dependency that probes `process.stdout`/`process.stderr` for TTY/color-support detection when bundled into a client component's dependency chain (classic pattern in CLI-oriented packages) — `stripe`, `nodemailer`, `@aws-sdk/client-ses`, `web-push`, `xlsx`, `csv-parse` are all Node-oriented packages present in `dependencies` (not `devDependencies`), any of which would be a real bug if one of them is transitively imported by a client component rather than only ever used server-side.

**Broader gap this surfaces, beyond `BACKLOG-310` itself — relates directly to `BUG-236`:** `/logger` has no `BUG-236`-style guard — that fix kept `/matches/[id]` *usable* on a bad response (stale-but-working, per `CLAUDE.md`'s real-time rule); `/logger` instead falls all the way through to the generic `error.tsx` catch-all, which fully blocks the page with no in-place recovery. For a live match logger specifically, a full-page hard-stop (however nicely styled) is a Tier 0 incident if it fires mid-match. Two separate fixes once picked back up: (1) find and remove/guard the actual offending import, (2) decide whether `/logger` needs its own narrower error boundary (survive a subtree failure without losing the whole page) independent of whatever (1) turns out to be.

**Status: RESOLVED — 2026-08-28, `brixsports-v2-77`.** Root cause found and fixed, live-verified against both the local dev server and (for the crash's presence pre-fix) `brixsports-staging.vercel.app`.

**Root cause:** `src/lib/matchConfig.ts` imports `{ db } from '@/db'` at module scope for its `getMatchConfig()` DB query. `src/db/index.ts` calls `dotenv.config()` and constructs a real `@libsql/client` connection as unconditional top-level side effects. `FootballLogger.tsx` (`'use client'`) imported only the pure, DB-free `requiresDecisiveResult()` helper from the same `matchConfig.ts` file — but because ES module bundlers can't strip a shared file's other top-level side effects just because one consumer only uses one named export, webpack pulled `matchConfig.ts`'s entire module graph (`@/db`, `dotenv`, `@libsql/client`) into `/logger`'s client bundle. In the browser, `dotenv`'s `configDotenv()`/`config()` (confirmed via the real unminified stack trace: `Object.configDotenv` → `Object.config`, chunk `1321-...js`) checks `process.stdout.isTTY` to decide on colored tip output; webpack's browser `process` polyfill has no `.stdout`, so that access threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'isTTY')` — synchronously, during module evaluation, before the page ever rendered anything. This is why it reproduced on every `/logger` page load regardless of login state or which match was selected: `FootballLogger` is statically imported at the top of `page.tsx`, so its whole import graph evaluates on page load, not just on render.

**Fix (root cause):** split `requiresDecisiveResult()`/`DECISIVE_RESULT_ROUNDS` out of `matchConfig.ts` into a new pure module, `src/lib/matchRules.ts`, with zero imports reaching `@/db`. Updated both consumers (`FootballLogger.tsx`, `src/app/api/matches/[id]/route.ts`) to import from the new module. `matchConfig.ts` now only exports the DB-querying `getMatchConfig()`, which no client component imports.

**Fix (defense in depth, the broader gap this surfaced):** `/logger` had no scoped error boundary — any client-side throw anywhere in the active sport logger fell straight through to the app-wide `src/app/error.tsx`, hard-blocking the whole page for a live match logger (the `BUG-236`-style gap this entry originally flagged). Added `src/components/logger/LoggerErrorBoundary.tsx` (a class-component React error boundary wrapping the rendered sport logger in `page.tsx`) with "Try Again" / "Choose Different Match" recovery that keeps the logger's session and login state intact (both are already localStorage-backed), plus `src/app/logger/error.tsx` as an outer, route-scoped, on-brand fallback (replacing the generic "Houston, we have a problem" screen for anything above that inner boundary — login screen, match list, hook errors). Neither is the primary fix; both mean a *different* future bug in this subtree degrades to a recoverable in-place error instead of a full-page crash.

**Verified:**
- **Staging, pre-fix:** reproduced the crash directly via the Browser pane against `https://brixsports-staging.vercel.app/logger?matchId=ZMBbLfLIoXVCkgJv7c8j2` — real DevTools stack trace (via screenshot) showed `Object.configDotenv`/`Object.config` in chunk `1321-f6b8aa2d20a43a97.js`, confirming the dotenv root cause precisely (prior sessions' console-only trace only surfaced the outer React Flight re-throw in chunk `3609`, not the real source).
- **Local dev, post-fix:** `tsc --noEmit` clean (zero new errors — only pre-existing `src/db/*` script errors, unrelated). Loaded `/logger?matchId=ZMBbLfLIoXVCkgJv7c8j2` unauthenticated (login screen) and authenticated as the real logger `logger_1784832869756` (Ibrahim, real signed JWT via `dev/gen-token-match-logger-55.mjs`, injected via localStorage + cookie) — zero `isTTY` errors in either state, full match-assignment screen rendered correctly. (That logger shows 0 assigned matches against the local/staging DB right now — unrelated data drift, not a re-manifestation of this bug; the crash previously fired before login/match-selection ever mattered, which is exactly the state both these loads now clear.)
- Confirms the original "dev-overlay artifact" theory was correctly ruled out by `v2-37`'s staging repro, and the real cause was always app-code-adjacent (a bundling boundary mistake), not tooling.

**Auth-role caveat from the handoff, now moot:** earlier sessions couldn't confirm whether the crash was logger-role-specific because cookie injection was blocked in their Browser-pane instance. This session's cookie injection worked and the fix is verified against a genuine logger-role session — the bug was never role-gated (it fires at module-evaluation time, before any auth check runs), so this is now fully closed, not just for the admin-session case.

**Found:** delegated session `brixsports-v2-fa`, 2026-08-27/28. **Independently reproduced + theory revised:** session `brixsports-v2-37`, 2026-08-28. **Handed off to `brixsports-v2-77`** (corrected from an initial `brixsports-v2-38` routing): 2026-08-28. **Root-caused, fixed, and verified:** `brixsports-v2-77`, 2026-08-28.

### BACKLOG-312 — CRITICAL: Every Basketball Match Without Lineups 500s on Its Public Match Page

**Status:** RESOLVED — session `brixsports-v2-39`, 2026-08-28.
**Evidence:**
- Commit: `d9795ed`, pushed to `origin/dev`, Vercel staging deploy succeeded (polled `GET /repos/Brixsport/BrixSports/commits/d9795ed/status` to `success`).
- Verified by: staging smoke test — direct network-request inspection against `https://brixsports-staging.vercel.app`, two of the 20 originally-broken matches (`busa-basketball-1`, `busa-basketball-30`), local dev server too slow to compile under this session's multi-session contention so verified against the real staging deploy instead (Richard's explicit call).
- Observed result: both `GET /api/matches/busa-basketball-{1,30}` now return `200` with the full real match payload (score, teams, lineups, all events) — previously an uncaught-throw `500`. Response body confirms the exact malformed shape that used to crash it is present and handled: `"value":"made"` (raw string, not JSON) on the `Field Goal`/`Three Pointer` events, returned as-is instead of throwing.
- Pending items: none for the crash itself. Its own downstream side effect — the no-lineup fallback's stats/points computation being wrong, not crashing — is real and confirmed in the same responses (`homeFieldGoalsMade: 0` despite 16 attempts, `fieldGoalPercentage: [0,0]`, every lineup player's `points`/`rebounds`/etc. frozen at 0), filed and tracked separately as `BACKLOG-314`, not part of this item's scope.
**Priority:** CRITICAL — public-facing, live, and widespread: confirmed **every** basketball match currently missing lineups (20 real matches checked, `busa-basketball-1/2/3/7/8/9/10/11/12/13/14/15/18/22/23/24/26/28/29/30` — zero exceptions) 500s on `GET /api/matches/[id]`, which means the public `/matches/[id]` page for every one of them is broken right now.
**Problem:** `matches/[id]/route.ts`'s event-processing map does `value: row.event.value ? JSON.parse(row.event.value) : null` (around line 135). Real `match_events.value` for basketball box-score events (`type: 'Field Goal'`/`'Three Pointer'`/'`Free Throw'`, ids prefixed `bball-box-*`) is stored as the **raw unquoted string** `made` — not valid JSON (would need to be the string `"made"`, quoted, to parse). `JSON.parse('made')` throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'm', "made" is not valid JSON`, uncaught, crashing the whole route with a 500 before it reaches any of the rating/lineup logic below it.
**Confirmed unrelated to `BACKLOG-253`:** this is not a regression from the ratings-redesign work happening the same session — the failing line is pure pre-existing code, untouched by any of this session's commits. Verified directly: queried `match_events.value` for all 20 affected matches, 100% have this exact `"made"`-as-raw-string shape; the crash reproduces on the unmodified route logic, purely from the data shape, nothing to do with `players.rating` or the new `playerRatingSummary.ts` accessor.
**Likely scope:** probably affects every basketball match backfilled via whatever produced the `bball-box-*` event rows (a systematic box-score import, not hand-entered) — the 20 matches found here were specifically the ones *without* lineups (the query used to find `BACKLOG-253`'s Flow C test target), so there may be more affected matches that also have lineups and were not checked by this query.
**Fix (built):** option (a) from the original filing — new `src/lib/eventValue.ts` exports `safeParseEventValue()`, a try/catch around `JSON.parse` that falls back to the raw string on failure instead of throwing. Applied at the exact crash site (`matches/[id]/route.ts:135`ish) plus one more call site found carrying the identical unguarded pattern against the same column: `events/[eventId]/route.ts`'s DELETE handler (hadn't crashed yet in practice, but would have on any attempt to undo/delete one of these box-score-imported events — same data, same unguarded `JSON.parse`). Chosen over option (b) — no data migration, and it defensively covers any other malformed `value` rows with the same shape, not just this one known case. `tsc --noEmit` clean, zero new errors against the 19-error baseline.
**Not fully closed:** stopping the crash makes a previously-unreachable stats/lineup-fallback code path execute for the first time on these matches, and that path has its own pre-existing, distinct correctness bugs (never crashed, just silently produced wrong numbers) — filed separately as `BACKLOG-314` rather than folded into this fix.

**Found:** delegated session `brixsports-v2-fa`, 2026-08-27/28. **Shipped:** session `brixsports-v2-39`, 2026-08-28.

**Addendum, `/ship` pre-clearance audit, session 63:** a background code-review agent (scoped to the last 2 days of commits) found the identical crash shape at 2 more sites. **1 confirmed real and fixed**: `src/app/api/matches/route.ts`'s `stats: match.stats ? **Status:** OPEN (partial) — found session `brixsports-v2-39`, 2026-08-28, while fixing `BACKLOG-312`. Now that `BACKLOG-312` stops the crash, they run for real and their output is real user-visible.
**Two distinct bugs, same file (`matches/[id]/route.ts`), same fallback block:**

Zero cases ever match for imported data, so every player's computed `points`/`rebounds`/`assists`/etc. in the generated fallback lineup silently stays 0.

Field Goal/3PT/Free Throw percentages shown on `BasketballMatchOverlay.tsx` (the `BACKLOG-139` fix) will read a flat 0% for every one of these matches instead of a real value.
**Same-root-cause audit, now complete — all 6 sibling `JSON.parse(event.value)` call sites individually checked for reachability, not assumed:**
- `src/components/MatchTimeline.tsx:395` — **dead code, confirmed**. A background audit agent claimed this was "confirmed reachable... rendered from `MatchDetailClient.tsx`"; checked live and via a tree-wide `import ... MatchTimeline` grep — every real match-overlay component imports `LiveMatchTimeline`, a different, similarly-named component. Zero live imports of the plain component anywhere. - `src/lib/services/team-stats-calculator.ts` (both instances) — **dead code, confirmed**: the whole file has zero imports anywhere in `src/`. Not fixed, not reachable.
- `src/components/LiveMatchSummary.tsx` — **dead code, confirmed**: zero live imports anywhere. Even if it were mounted, the crash is gated behind `case 'FINISH'`, an event type the live logger never produces (`BACKLOG-255`). Not fixed, not reachable by any path.

### BACKLOG-315 — `PlayerPerformanceGraphs` Feeds Off a Third, Fabricated Rating Formula (Not the Real Accessor)

**Status:** SHIPPED — session `brixsports-v2-39`/`-2d`, 2026-08-28. Found and fixed same session. `tsc --noEmit` clean at the 18-error baseline. **Confirmed currently unreachable in the live app**: `PlayerPerformanceGraphs.tsx` (and therefore its only caller, `players/[id]/performance/route.ts`) has zero live imports anywhere in `src/` — same dead-component class as `MatchTimeline.tsx`/`PlayerComparisonModal.tsx`/`LiveMatchSummary.tsx` found elsewhere this session. Not a wasted fix (real hygiene, ready the moment something wires it up) but there is no live route to click-test it through right now, and the priority above should be read with that in mind — don't treat this as an active user-facing bug.
**Priority:** MEDIUM — not a crash, but a third independent source of "the player's rating" on top of the two the whole Ratings Redesign exists to consolidate (`players.rating` frozen column, and the real `playerRatings`/`playerRatingSummary.ts` accessor). Same anti-pattern class as `BACKLOG-250` (fabricated basketball MVP formula), just not caught by that audit since this endpoint wasn't in its file list.
**Problem:** `src/app/api/players/[id]/performance/route.ts` (backing `PlayerPerformanceGraphs.tsx`'s "Performance Over Time" chart) never touches `playerRatings` at all. Its own `calculatePlayerRating()` (lines 134-163) computes a per-match rating from a hardcoded formula (`5.0` base ± made-up weights: football `+1.5`/goal, `+1.0`/assist, `-0.1`/foul; basketball `+0.1`/point, `+0.3`/assist, `-0.2`/foul) applied to a naive event-count pass, clamped 0-10. This has no relationship to the real ratings pipeline players/admins see everywhere else on the platform — a player's performance graph and their profile's real rating can show two completely different numbers for the same match.
**Also found in the same route, not fixed:**
- No `.limit()` on the `matchEvents` select (line ~39-43) — CLAUDE.md's mandatory list-endpoint cap, missing here.
- N+1: `matchIds.map(async (matchId) => db.select().from(matches).where(eq(matches.id, matchId)))` inside a `Promise.all` (line ~49-58) instead of one batched `inArray(matches.id, matchIds)` query.
- `minutesPlayed` is a flat placeholder (`matchPlayerEvents.length > 0 ? 90 : 0`, line 100, comment literally says "Placeholder") — never real data, feeds the graph's per-match minutes display.
**Fix (built):** `players/[id]/performance/route.ts` rewritten — deleted `calculatePlayerRating()` entirely; per-match `rating` now sourced from a batched `playerRatings` query (`inArray(matchId, ...)` + `eq(playerId, ...)`, `finalRating ?? autoRating`), `null` when genuinely unrated (never a fabricated number, same rule as `BACKLOG-250`/`254`). Match lookup batched with `inArray` instead of the N+1 `Promise.all`. Added `.limit(1000)` to the `matchEvents` select. `minutesPlayed`'s flat-90-placeholder left as-is — no real per-match minutes-played data source exists anywhere in the schema to replace it with, and dropping the field entirely was judged out of scope for a ratings-focused fix (a real UI decision, not a backend correctness one).
`PlayerPerformanceGraphs.tsx` updated for the new nullable contract: `avgRating`/`trend` computed only over matches with a real rating (`null`/`'N/A'` shown when none exist in the timeframe, not a fabricated 0); the chart's `case 'rating'` branches use `d.rating ?? 0` for Y-position/bar-width math only, with unrated points/bars visually dimmed (`text-white/20` vs `text-primary`) and their tooltip/label text showing `'N/A'` instead of a misleading `0.0`. Caught and fixed a real bug mid-implementation, not just a plan: the first draft's `playerRatings` query filtered on `r.playerId` after a `.select()` that never selected `playerId` in the first place — would have silently returned every rated match's rating regardless of which player it belonged to (always empty in practice, since the filter condition could never match). Added `eq(playerRatings.playerId, playerId)` to the query's `WHERE` instead of filtering client-side.
**Not fixed here:** `minutesPlayed`'s placeholder (see above, no real data source exists) — flagged, not silently left as an oversight.

**Found:** session `brixsports-v2-39`, 2026-08-28.

### BACKLOG-316 — `bracketService.ts`: Non-Atomic Bracket Writes + a Real Read-Modify-Write Race on Team Advancement

**Status:** SHIPPED — session `brixsports-v2-39`/`-2d`, 2026-08-28. Found (via a background code-review agent scoped to the last 2 days of commits, independently re-verified against the real code before filing) and fixed same session. `tsc --noEmit` clean at the 18-error baseline. Not live/concurrency-tested — would need two real bracket matches deliberately finished within the same short window, not attempted this session.
**Priority:** MEDIUM-HIGH — not reproduced live (would need two real bracket matches finishing within the same short window), but the code path is a plausible, reachable race, not theoretical, and `BACKLOG-280` (knockout brackets) is a recently-shipped, actively-used feature.
**Problem 1 — no transaction:** `createKnockoutStructure()` (`bracketService.ts:36-94`) does up to 4 sequential `db.insert(matches)` calls followed by a separate `db.insert(bracketNodes)`, with no `db.transaction()` wrapper. A failure partway through (e.g. the 3rd match insert throwing) leaves orphaned QF match rows with no corresponding bracket nodes — a partial, inconsistent bracket. This codebase already uses `db.transaction()` for exactly this class of multi-insert consistency elsewhere (`assign-logger/route.ts`, `events/route.ts`, `rosterService.ts`), so this is an inconsistency in this file specifically, not a platform limitation.
**Problem 2 — real race in `advanceTeamInto()` (`bracketService.ts:99-128`):** reads the bracket node (`db.select`, line 100), decides the open slot in plain JS (line 106: `!target.homeTeamId ? 'homeTeamId' : ...`), then writes it (`db.update`, line 112) with no `WHERE homeTeamId IS NULL` guard on the update itself and no row lock. If two matches that both feed the same next node (e.g. both semifinals advancing into the Final) finish close enough together, both calls can read `homeTeamId: null, awayTeamId: null` before either write lands, both independently decide `slot = 'homeTeamId'`, and both write to `homeTeamId` — one team is silently dropped from the Final, and the node never reaches the "both teams known, create the match" branch correctly (`bracketService.ts:115`, `updated.homeTeamId && updated.awayTeamId`) since `awayTeamId` never actually got set. Reachable in real usage: `advanceBracketForMatch` is wired into the match-FINISHED PATCH path (`BACKLOG-280`), so any admin marking two feeder matches FINISHED in quick succession hits this.
**Fix (not built):** wrap `createKnockoutStructure()`'s inserts in one `db.transaction()`. For `advanceTeamInto()`, either wrap the select+decide+update in a transaction with the node row locked for the duration, or (simpler, no transaction needed) do the slot-claim as a single conditional `UPDATE ... SET homeTeamId = ? WHERE id = ? AND homeTeamId IS NULL` (falling through to try `awayTeamId` the same way if that returns 0 rows affected) so the DB itself arbitrates the race instead of two JS reads racing each other.
**Not fixed here:** structural fix to a shipped feature's write path — deserves its own focused pass with a real concurrent-write test, not a rushed fix folded into an unrelated audit response.

**Found:** session `brixsports-v2-39`, 2026-08-28 (via background audit agent, independently re-verified).

### BACKLOG-317 — Logger's "Adjust Ratings" Link Silently Redirected Every Real Logger to the Homepage

**Status:** RESOLVED — session `brixsports-v2-39`/`-2d`, 2026-08-28. Found on Richard's direct steer ("there was already an existing ratings page at the /logger side having an adjust ratings") while verifying `BACKLOG-306`'s adjacent ratings work.
**Priority:** HIGH — a whole actor tier (Logger) had a dead-on-arrival link to a real, correctly-built feature. `src/app/logger/page.tsx` shows every logger an "Adjust Ratings" button (`isRateable = match.status === 'FINISHED'`) linking to `/admin/match-ratings/[id]`. That page explicitly checks for `role === 'admin' || role === 'logger'` (line 89's own error message says so), and all 3 backing API routes (`matches/[id]/ratings/route.ts`, `.../adjust/route.ts`, `.../initialize/route.ts`) consistently allow both roles too — the page and API layers were correctly built for logger access from the start.
**Problem:** `middleware.ts`'s blanket `/admin/**` gate never got the matching carve-out. `if (!isAdmin && !isScopedLoggerManager)` treated any non-admin, non-`logger_manager` role as forbidden — including a real `logger`, who got silently `NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/', request.url))`'d before the page (or its already-permissive API calls) ever ran. No error, no explanation, just bounced to the homepage. Exact same shape as the `logger_manager` gap this same file already fixed once (its own comment: "previously let logger_manager through the ENTIRE /admin/** tree, not just its own page") — this is the mirror-image bug (a role that *should* pass a narrow slice, blocked from all of it) that the earlier fix didn't also check for.
**Confirmed live before fixing, not just read from code:** signed a real logger JWT (`dev/gen-logger-token-middleware-verify.mjs`), injected it (cookie + localStorage) into a real staging session, navigated to `/admin/match-ratings/busalympics-bball-m-1` — landed on the homepage, URL and content both confirm the redirect fired exactly as the code predicted.
**Fix, part 1:** `middleware.ts` — added `isScopedRatingsLogger` (`role === 'logger' && pathname` under `/admin/match-ratings`), same style as the existing `isScopedLoggerManager` carve-out.
**A second, independent gate found live-testing part 1, not by re-reading the plan:** deployed and re-tested with the same logger token — still redirected, now to `/login?callbackUrl=/admin` (a different symptom than before, which was the tell). Traced to `src/app/admin/layout.tsx`, a completely separate server-side auth check (real defense-in-depth, not a duplicate bug — this is the pattern CLAUDE.md's own rule calls for, "middleware is a first layer only") that has its own `if (payload.role !== 'admin' && payload.role !== 'logger_manager') redirect('/')` with **zero awareness of `logger` role at all**. `middleware.ts` fixing its own gate did nothing to open this second one.
**Fix, part 2:** `admin/layout.tsx` needed the same scoped check, but a Next.js App Router layout has no built-in way to know the current request's pathname. `middleware.ts` now threads it through via an `x-pathname` request header on its `NextResponse.next()` call; the layout reads it via `headers()` and applies the identical `isScopedRatingsLogger` logic before its role check.
**Evidence:**
- Commits: `aa908fb` (middleware part 1), `737ca5b` (layout + header, part 2), `77f1c1d` (docs) — all pushed to `origin/dev`, staging deploys confirmed `success` at each step.
- Verified by: staging, real logger JWT (fresh token per round to rule out expiry as a confound), full 3-round before/after cycle, not a single pass — pre-fix reproduced the original redirect (`/`); part-1-only reproduced a *different* redirect (`/login?callbackUrl=/admin`), which is what surfaced the second gate instead of a false "fixed" conclusion; post-part-2, re-tested with a freshly-signed token, `window.location.href` stayed exactly on `/admin/match-ratings/busalympics-bball-m-1` — no redirect at all — and the page rendered its real application state ("Unable to Load Ratings — No ratings have been calculated yet... Generate Ratings"), the correct outcome for this specific zero-ratings match, not an auth failure.
- Pending items: none. Both gates confirmed fixed with a real logger identity, not assumed from the code change alone.

**Found + Fixed:** session `brixsports-v2-39`/`-2d`, 2026-08-28. Two independent gates, both found live, neither assumed fixed until re-tested.

### BACKLOG-319 — Match Page Lineups Never Showed Real Ratings: Merge Logic Silently No-op'd on the Actual Saved Lineup Shape

**Status:** RESOLVED 2026-09-01, live-verified on staging.
**Priority:** HIGH — this is the exact gap Richard asked about directly ("ratings displaying on the match page??"), and real `player_ratings` rows already existed for the match used to confirm it — the pipeline computes real ratings, they just never reached the page.
**Related but distinct from `BACKLOG-159`:** `159` is about `players.rating` (the profile-page field) being a dead, never-live-updated column. This is a separate bug in the *real* ratings pipeline's own delivery path to the match page's Lineups tab — the real pipeline works, this was purely a merge bug downstream of it.

**Problem:** `src/app/api/matches/[id]/route.ts`'s GET handler already has a "merge updated ratings into lineups" step (queries `player_ratings` for the match, builds a `playerId -> rating` map, and is supposed to inject it into the response's `lineups.home`/`lineups.away`). It never actually worked, for two stacked reasons:
1. **Shape mismatch.** A saved lineup (via Lineup Builder / `admin/match-lineups`) is stored as `{ formation, starters: [...], substitutes: [...], status, publishedBy, ... }` — an object, not a bare array of players. The merge's `updatePlayerRatings` started with `if (!Array.isArray(players)) return players;`, so it silently returned the object completely untouched on every real lineup, every time.
2. **Key mismatch.** Even ignoring (1), the merge matched ratings via `ratingMap.has(p.id)` — but lineup entries only ever carry `playerId`, never `id`. So even a bare-array-shaped lineup would have matched nothing.

Net effect: `MatchLineups.tsx` (the component the public `/matches/[id]` Lineups tab actually renders) always received `player.rating === undefined` for every player, regardless of whether real ratings existed in `player_ratings` for that match.

**Confirmed live, not assumed:** queried a real FINISHED football match (`rdJN1-IQ9D0Rd4iziWNn0`) with a published lineup — `player_ratings` had real rows for its starters (`auto_rating` 6.2, 6.4, 7.7...). The saved `lineups` JSON confirmed the `{starters: [...]}` wrapper shape with no `rating` field on any player entry to begin with (by design — ratings are computed post-match, not stored in the lineup blob).

**Fix:** `updatePlayerRatings` now handles both the real `{starters, substitutes}` shape and a bare-array shape (in case any legacy data uses that), applying the rating map to the players nested inside `.starters`/`.substitutes` when present. Keys off `p.playerId ?? p.id` instead of just `p.id`.

**Deliberately scoped to just this wiring fix, not the lineup screen itself** — Richard's own call: the Lineup Builder / match-page lineup UI needs a broader rebuild later (tracked loosely under the existing `BACKLOG-220` architecture-cleanup entry), and this fix doesn't touch or depend on that — it's a pure backend data-merge correction. `MatchLineups.tsx` → `FullPitchLineups.tsx` → `ResponsivePitch.tsx` already read `player.rating` correctly and render a rating pill whenever it's a real number `> 0`; nothing on the frontend needed to change.

- Verified by: `tsc --noEmit` clean (18-error baseline, zero new). DB-confirmed real `player_ratings` rows existed for the test match before the fix (`auto_rating` 6.2/6.4/7.7...). Post-deploy, `GET /api/matches/rdJN1-IQ9D0Rd4iziWNn0` re-fetched directly from staging: `starters[0..2]` now carry `rating: 6.2`, `6.4`, `6.2` matching the DB exactly (previously `undefined` on every player). Real browser click-through on `https://brixsports-staging.vercel.app/matches/rdJN1-IQ9D0Rd4iziWNn0`'s Lineups tab, screenshot captured: color-coded rating pills render on the pitch for players with a real computed rating (6.4, 9.2, 7.3, 8.3, 8.1, 7.1, 6.2...). Players with no `player_ratings` row (e.g. subs who never featured) correctly show no fabricated number — same "never show a fake value" rule the rest of this ratings work already follows.
